web_evidence.title: Read an excerpt of The Order — Daniel Silva
web_evidence.note: The author's official site supplies the sustained first chapter. An external narrator consistently calls Luigi Donati 'he,' reports his movements and history, and renders his thoughts without becoming a participating character.

web_evidence.title: The Order by Daniel Silva — Apple Books
web_evidence.note: The publisher description includes a short opening passage that externally narrates Gabriel and Chiara in third person; its brevity and catalog context limit its weight.

web_evidence.title: THE ORDER by Daniel Silva — pages 101–150
web_evidence.note: An informal interior reproduction shows sustained external narration of Gabriel, Donati, and Father Jordan in chapters 26–27, including the context surrounding sampled dialogue. It is useful corroboration but is not an authorized source.

person_note: The controlling prose is third person. The strongest evidence is the authorized first chapter, which sustains external narration of Donati while also accessing his thoughts. The Goodreads sample is dominated by dialogue and author's-note material, but q05054 independently exposes compatible third-person scene narration, and the located interior context continues that pattern across Gabriel, Donati, and Father Jordan. First-person forms in the sample belong to speech, cited documents, or authorial paratext, not an autonomous first-person narrative section. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base narration or person alternation was found; the only limitation is that the authorized excerpt covers the opening rather than the whole book.
